item.title: Bezos, Arnault, Premji Pour Money Into AI Humanoid Robot Startups
item.description: Family offices are particularly well-positioned to make these wagers.

item.title: Katayama Cites Bessent’s Faith in Japan’s Improving Fiscal Path
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sees Japan’s fiscal condition improving, according to Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama, who spoke after Bessent gave a series of interviews in the wake of Washington’s move to help Tokyo prop up the yen last week.

item.title: Circle Revenue Misses Estimates as Crypto Markets Mired in Rout
item.description: Circle Internet Group Inc. reported second-quarter revenue that missed Wall Street expectations after circulation of its stablecoin USDC fell from a peak amid a protracted slide in cryptocurrency markets.

item.title: Iran War Exposes US Military Aluminum Risk Shown in Pentagon War Game
item.description: Supplies of an ultra-refined form of the metal used in fighter jets are tight after drones damaged a UAE plant.

item.title: Yann LeCun Joins New AI Investing Firm 224 Ventures
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s former chief AI scientist Yann LeCun, often called one of the “godfathers of AI,” is joining a new venture firm to invest in artificial intelligence startups.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak: Why the Death Rate Is Rising as Patients Reach Care Too Late
item.description: The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak is becoming steadily deadlier on paper, as too many people reach treatment only after the disease has become critical.

item.title: Hyperscaler Debt Risks Europe’s Allure Morgan Stanley IM Says
item.description: European investment-grade credit’s relative appeal over the US would diminish if the region absorbs a lot more bond issuance from hyperscalers, according to a Morgan Stanley Investment Management Inc. strategist.

item.title: Tech Melt-Up Drives $3.5 Trillion Nasdaq 100 Rally in Four Days
item.description: A dramatic turnaround in technology stocks has powered a $3.5 trillion increase in the Nasdaq 100’s market capitalization in just four days, driven by strong earnings that have emboldened investors about the AI outlook.

item.title: Shein Is Said to Plan Gauging Investor Demand for Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Fast-fashion retailer Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is planning to start gauging investor demand for its Hong Kong initial public offering as soon as this week, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: India Rules Out Early End To FX Deposit Plan, Sees Healthy Flows
item.description: India is not considering an early closure of a program aimed at attracting deposits from the country’s 35-million-strong diaspora, with the central bank expecting robust inflows until the window shuts in end-September.

item.title: Sandisk Earnings Give Dip Buyers an Opening After Stock’s Plunge
item.description: Sandisk Corp.’s high flying stock tumbled back to Earth last month. Its earnings after the market closes Wednesday will test whether strong results are enough to entice investors to buy in again.

item.title: Why India’s New Closing Auction Is Confusing Traders: Q&A
item.description: India’s two equity bourses — the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. and BSE Ltd. — introduced on Monday an auction to determine the closing price of more than 200 stocks with derivatives contracts, replacing a decades-old methodology.

item.title: Barclays, HSBC Say Warsh Makes Inflation-Linked Debt Appeal
item.description: Barclays Plc and HSBC Holdings Plc say concern the Federal Reserve is dragging its feet on inflation is giving investors another reason to buy bonds that offer protection from accelerating price growth.

item.title: Brazil Central Bank to Cut Interest Rate to 14%
item.description: A string of benign inflation reports in Brazil has cemented market bets on another interest rate cut this month and prompted some economists to consider further monetary easing this year.

item.title: LIC Share Sale Sees Tepid Retail Demand After India Upsized Deal
item.description: Retail investors largely stayed on the sidelines in India’s share sale in Life Insurance Corp., signaling uneven demand a day after strong bids from institutions led the government to increase the offering’s size to $3.3 billion.

item.title: UK in Longest Jobs Slump Since Financial Crisis, PMI Shows
item.description: Britain’s two-year jobs market downturn has lasted as long as the slump seen during the global financial crisis as firms cut costs and turn to artificial intelligence, according to a closely watched survey.

item.title: US Ban on Chinese Optical Parts Hurts Hyperscalers, Report Says
item.description: A potential ban on the import of Chinese optical transceiver modules into the US would inflict collateral damage on US hyperscalers, exacerbating a supply bottleneck that no American firm can ease, research firm Counterpoint warned on Wednesday.

item.title: German Industry Builds Resilience to Low Rhine Levels, Bloomberg Economics Says
item.description: German industry has regularly faced low water levels in the Rhine river, leading to workarounds that could cushion the economic impact this time, according to Bloomberg Economics.

item.title: Taiyo Yuden Raises Earnings Forecast, Capex Plans on AI Demand
item.description: Taiyo Yuden Co., a maker of a key component used in AI data centers, boosted its full-year earnings outlook by 50% to above estimates and said it’s speeding up production capacity expansion plans to meet accelerating demand.

item.title: Italy Must Use EU’s Energy Leeway, Giorgetti Tells Lawmakers
item.description: Italy Finance Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti told lawmakers that he plans to use extra budget leeway authorized by the European Union for energy-related measures.

item.title: Australia Doubles Down on Data Centers Using Renewable Power
item.description: Australia’s federal government will press on with a nationwide push to ensure new data centers use renewable energy, pledging to pass laws despite opposition to the move from some regional administrations.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Hon Hai’s Sales Rise 54% on Strong AI Demand
item.description: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. reported a 54.2% increase in monthly sales, signaling sustained demand in global AI infrastructure buildout by customers such as Nvidia Corp.

item.title: Czech Inflation Quickens With Central Bank Set to Hold Rates
item.description: Inflation in the Czech Republic accelerated in July but remained below the central bank’s target, bolstering expectations that interest rates will stay on hold this week.

item.title: Schaeffler Targets 1,300 Job Cuts With Early Pension Push
item.description: Schaeffler AG plans to cut its German workforce through an expanded phased-retirement program as weak automotive demand continues to pressure the supplier.

item.title: Moove Hits $2.1 Billion Valuation in Mubadala-Led Fundraising
item.description: Moove has closed a $250 million investment round led by Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala, which will help the vehicle-financing and fleet-management startup add services for self-driving cars and expand into new geographies.

item.title: Glencore Has Taken a Provision on Radiant World Exposure
item.description: Glencore Plc said it has taken a provision on its exposure to iron ore trader Radiant World but that the exposure was not material to the company.

item.title: Moonshot Backer Monolith Seeks to Raise $500 Million in New Fund
item.description: Monolith Management, which backed artificial intelligence sensation Moonshot, wants to raise $500 million for a new fund focused on Chinese AI, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Honda Raises Outlook 30% as Weak Yen, US Demand Lift Profits
item.description: Honda Motor Co. raised its profit outlook after the motorcycle business, a weak yen and US demand for hybrids lifted quarterly results to a record.

item.title: Vietnam’s Techcombank Seeks $1 Billion, Joining Rush for Funds
item.description: Vietnam Technological and Commercial JSB, known as Techcombank, is seeking a $1 billion loan for regular business operations, according to people familiar with the matter, in what would be one of the Southeast Asian nation’s largest debt deals this year.

item.title: Next Lifts Outlook as UK’s Hot Summer Boosts Clothing Sales
item.description: Next Plc raised its outlook for the third time this fiscal year, after sales surged in the second quarter due to warm UK weather and pent-up demand in the Middle East and northern Europe.
